Description: This course introduces students to the properties, uses, and testing of common construction materials including concrete, timber, brick, and steel, alongside the methods used in building construction.
LearningOutcomes: Identify and describe the physical and mechanical properties of common construction materials.
Select appropriate construction materials for specific building applications based on performance criteria.
Conduct basic material testing procedures and interpret the results.

Description: Students learn to produce and interpret architectural and engineering drawings for building projects, as well as to prepare Bills of Quantities and cost estimates for construction works.
LearningOutcomes: Produce accurate architectural drawings to recognised standards using both manual and digital tools.
Interpret working drawings and specifications for construction projects.
Prepare basic Bills of Quantities and material cost estimates for small-scale building works.

Description: This course covers the fundamental principles of structural analysis and design, focusing on load distribution, beam and column behaviour, and the structural performance of common construction systems.
LearningOutcomes: Analyse forces acting on structural elements including beams, columns, and slabs.
Apply structural design principles to verify the adequacy of simple structural members.
Interpret structural drawings and relate them to construction site activities.

Description: An introductory course covering the theory of operation of motor vehicle systems, including the engine, transmission, braking, and electrical systems, with practical workshop activities.
LearningOutcomes: Describe the operating principles of the main motor vehicle systems and their components.
Perform routine vehicle inspection and maintenance tasks following manufacturer specifications.
Apply workshop safety practices and use tools and equipment correctly.

Description: This course develops students' skills in diagnosing and repairing engine faults using both traditional and electronic diagnostic methods, covering petrol and diesel engines commonly found in Zambia.
LearningOutcomes: Use diagnostic tools and scan equipment to identify engine faults accurately.
Carry out engine overhaul procedures including component measurement and replacement.
Interpret technical service manuals and apply manufacturer repair procedures.

Description: This course introduces students to the principles of agricultural engineering, covering soil mechanics, farm power sources, and the role of engineering in supporting food production in Zambia.
LearningOutcomes: Explain the role of agricultural engineering in improving farm productivity and food security.
Identify and describe different sources of farm power and their applications.
Analyse basic soil properties and their implications for agricultural engineering works.

Description: Students study the operation, maintenance, and management of farm machinery and equipment, including tractors, tillage implements, planting machines, and harvesting equipment.
LearningOutcomes: Describe the operating principles and components of common farm machinery.
Perform routine maintenance and servicing tasks on tractors and farm implements.
Select appropriate machinery for specific agricultural operations based on field and crop conditions.

Description: This elective course covers the principles of irrigation system design and water management for agricultural production, including drip, sprinkler, and surface irrigation methods relevant to Zambian agriculture.
LearningOutcomes: Design a basic irrigation system for a small-scale farm considering water availability and crop requirements.
Calculate irrigation scheduling requirements based on evapotranspiration and soil moisture data.
Evaluate the environmental and economic impacts of different irrigation methods.
